title: ZK-Hammer: Leaking Secrets from Zero-Knowledge Proofs via Rowhammer
problem: Zero-knowledge SNARK schemes are assumed cryptographically secure but their vulnerability to fault injection attacks via Rowhammer is unexplored, potentially compromising secret exponents.
motivation: SNARK schemes are widely deployed in verified computation; understanding their vulnerability to physical attacks is critical for secure system design.
method: ZK-Hammer uses a hardware vulnerability called Rowhammer (repeatedly accessing memory to flip bits in nearby locations) to corrupt the variables used in the mathematical calculations of zk-SNARK proofs—a type of cryptographic proof scheme designed to hide secrets. It targets the exponentiation step in the proof's mathematical representation (called a Quadratic Arithmetic Program). By analyzing these deliberately corrupted proofs using bilinear pairings (a cryptographic technique that works with pairs of values in a special mathematical structure), the attack recovers the secret parameters that should have remained hidden.
key_novelty: ZK-SNARK cryptographic proofs, which were thought to be secure, can be broken by Rowhammer attacks (hardware faults that flip bits in memory during calculations), allowing recovery of the secret parameters.
contributions: First successful Rowhammer attack on zk-SNARK implementations
Method to exploit QAP variables and recover secrets via bilinear pairing analysis
Demonstrates practical vulnerability of zero-knowledge proof systems to physical attacks
limitations: Attack limited to specific SNARK schemes; mitigation strategies not discussed.
primary_theme: Rowhammer-based side-channel attack on zero-knowledge proofs
